sections.h2: Who sets and collects property tax in Luzerne County
sections.html:
The county Assessment Office decides what each parcel is worth. The municipality and school district where the parcel sits then multiply that value by their own millage rates, and the result is your bill.

With 76 municipalities and a dozen school districts in the county, the list of districts is long: Wilkes-Barre Area, Hazleton Area, Wyoming Valley West, Pittston Area, Dallas, Crestwood, Greater Nanticoke Area, Hanover Area, Lake-Lehman, Northwest Area, Wyoming Area and Berwick Area. Two houses with the same assessment can therefore carry different yearly bills. Read the taxing bodies off your bill before you compare your house with one in the next town.

The Assessor's Office is in the Courthouse Annex at 153 North River Street, Wilkes-Barre, phone 570-825-1540. Hours are Monday to Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. A Hazleton branch keeps Tuesday and Thursday hours from 10:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. Mail for the appeals board goes to 200 North River Street, Wilkes-Barre, PA 18711.

File the county's appeal form with the Board of Assessment Appeals, along with a check payable to the County of Luzerne for the amount on the county's appeal filing fee schedule. The county then mails written notice of the hearing date, time and place. There are separate forms for single-family homes, multi-family residential property and vacant land.

The single-family form asks for what a board wants to see:

  • The tax map identification number, with map, block and lot.
  • The purchase date and price, plus a copy of the current deed.
  • The assessment under appeal, split between land and improvements, and your own opinion of market value.
  • Annual rent, if the property is rented.
  • Your reasons for the appeal, signed under penalty for false statements.

By filing you agree to a hearing and a decision after October 31, and one, two or three board members may hear the case. The board can raise an assessment as well as lower it, so a weak appeal can backfire. Call the Assessment Office for this year's filing deadline before you start. Gather your deed and your purchase paperwork first, since the form asks for both, and keep a copy of everything you file. Notice of the hearing arrives by mail, so make sure the office has your current address.

The Assessment Office takes delinquent property tax payments at the courthouse but does not issue tax bills. If you are paying back taxes in person, go to the Tax Claim Bureau first. It issues a statement for the amount you are paying. Only cash and checks are accepted for these payments, not credit cards.

Unpaid taxes can end in a tax sale. County ordinance describes four kinds: upset, private, judicial free and clear, and repository sales. The Tax Claim Bureau or its agent runs them under the Pennsylvania Real Estate Tax Sale Law (72 P.S. 5860.101 and following). Since March 1, 2026 the bureau or its agent collects a $100.00 fee from every buyer at a tax sale, and the county sheriff collects the same amount at mortgage foreclosure sales. The money goes into a county Demolition and Rehabilitation Fund for blighted buildings. Sales to nonprofits, land banks and government bodies are excluded.

County Council adopted Ordinance 2026-08 on May 26, 2026 by an 11 to 0 vote. It imposes the $15.00 fee that Act 152 of 2016 allows on every deed and mortgage recorded in the county. The money goes into a separate Luzerne County Demolition Fund, used only to tear down blighted property. The county must send the state Department of Community and Economic Development a plan within 90 days and a report each year after that.

The ordinance treats a property as blighted when it meets at least three of the criteria in section 5(d)(5) of the state's Abandoned and Blighted Property Conservatorship Act. It took effect 15 days after adoption, and the Recorder began collecting the amount on July 1, 2026. As a seller you will see it as one more line on the settlement statement.

Luzerne County has 135,055 households and 151,965 housing units. The county issued 295 building permits in 2025, and 89.3 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier. The estimated population was 332,126 in July 2025, up 2.0 percent from the 2020 base.

sections.h2: Property tax and transfer costs at closing
sections.html:
A Luzerne County closing carries three county-level costs on top of the tax bill itself.

  • Recording: the Recorder of Deeds schedule effective November 17, 2025 sets $72.75 for a deed or mortgage, and an extra $15.00 has applied to deeds and mortgages since July 1, 2026 for the county demolition fund.
  • PIN certification: the Assessor's Office certifies the parcel number on every deed and bills its own fee. Call 570-825-1525 for the amount.
  • Transfer tax: the county's schedule lists a 2 percent total in most municipalities, 3.5 percent in Wilkes-Barre and Pittston, and 2.5 percent in Kingston Borough. Hazleton's total is 2 percent.

The purchase agreement decides who pays the transfer tax, though both parties are liable to the state, so read that clause before you accept an offer.

The year's real estate tax is also divided between seller and buyer. Ask your closing agent how the split is figured, and check that the bill used is for the right municipality and school district.

If you are selling a house with taxes owed, ask the Tax Claim Bureau for a payoff statement. Give it to the title company so every open year is listed and paid out of your proceeds at settlement. Paying the balance before a tax sale date keeps the county from forcing a sale of the house. Anything owed to the county is taken out of your proceeds at the table, so you walk away with the rest.

One more call is worth making: ask your municipal office about any sewer, garbage or permit items tied to your address. Those are billed separately from the county tax.

faqs.q: Who do I call to dispute my Luzerne County assessment?
faqs.a: Call the Assessor's Office at 570-825-1540 or file the appeal form with the Board of Assessment Appeals. Include the filing fee check made out to the County of Luzerne.

faqs.q: Where do I pay delinquent Luzerne County property taxes?
faqs.a: Pay at the courthouse after stopping first at the Tax Claim Bureau, which issues the statement. Only cash and checks are accepted, and credit cards are not.

faqs.q: What is the transfer tax in Wilkes-Barre?
faqs.a: The Recorder of Deeds schedule lists a 3.5 percent total for Wilkes-Barre. Most other municipalities show 2 percent, and Kingston Borough shows 2.5 percent.

faqs.q: Does Luzerne County charge a fee at tax sales?
faqs.a: Yes. Since March 1, 2026 a $100.00 fee is added to the purchase price at tax sales and mortgage foreclosure sales, paid by the buyer into the demolition and rehabilitation fund.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Luzerne County?
faqs.a: The median value of owner-occupied homes is $174,100 for 2020 to 2024. Individual towns can differ widely from that figure.
